newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT ENDS DAY OF CONSOLIDATION UP A NOTCH.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT ENDS DAY OF CONSOLIDATION UP A NOTCH.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil saw a slight recovery just before the close on Monday after a fairly uninspiring days trade, brokers said.
September Brent on the IPE closed up 10 cents at $18.58 a barrel in what brokers saw as a consolidation following the losses seen at the end of last week.
On Friday the prompt Brent contract slid 42 cents.
"We've just been consolidating today. It's been very boring and we saw a moderate recovery at the end from some MOC (market on close) buying," one said.

Traders had mixed views on short term market direction. Some expected prices to fall further and pointed to a well supplied local North Sea market and the fundamental weakness to come as Iraqi crude of up to 1.5 million barrels per day starts to flow in the next few days.
Others said that level of Iraqi crude exports was already factored into the outright price and that technically the market looked strong and predicted a slow move up over the next few days.
"We had the Iraqi headlines today and no-one batted an eye. It's all there already and will only affect the differentials of the (crude) grades it displaces," a European refiner said.
Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Monday that his country should start exporting crude witin the next few days.
NYMEX gasoline ended the day lower as NYMEX locals sold the September gasoline-to-WTI crude crack spreads.
Brokers expected August gas oil to start Tuesday steady from Monday's $168 close. This represented a loss of $1.50 on the day.
"We could see it go either way tomorrow - it's expiry and no-one really knows what to expect," one said.
The August gas oil contract expires at noon on Tuesday.
